question: Which of these is NOT a job of a professional nursing organization when it comes to ethics?

options.A: Promoting values like patient autonomy and justice
options.B: Drafting and updating the code of ethics for the profession
options.C: Issuing personal loans to nurses in financial distress
options.D: Guiding members on how to handle moral dilemmas

explanation: Professional bodies write our ethical codes and help us navigate tough clinical choices, but they don't operate as financial banks or loan providers. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T5#GNS112_U1_T5_h4)

question: What is the primary purpose of irrigating a fresh wound with normal saline?

options.A: To wash away bacteria and loose debris
options.B: To numb the pain temporarily
options.C: To close the skin edges tightly
options.D: To stop bleeding from large arteries

explanation: High-volume fluid irrigation physically flushes out contaminants that could otherwise cause a localized infection. [learn more](GNS311_U4_T3#GNS311_U4_T3_h3)

question: When assessing a patient's supplement use, which detail is MOST important to record?

options.A: The color and shape of the retail cardboard packaging
options.B: The political affiliation of the supplement manufacturer
options.C: The exact product name, dosage, and frequency of intake
options.D: The name of the transport vehicle used to deliver the pills

explanation: Knowing the exact name and dose helps you and the medical team spot potential drug clashes right away. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T014#GNS227_U7_T014_h6)

question: What is the main goal of evaluation in nursing?

options.A: To determine how well objectives or standards have been met
options.B: To replace daily nursing shift reports
options.C: To increase the cost of healthcare services
options.D: To punish students or staff for clinical errors

explanation: Evaluation is simply checking our work against set standards to see if we reached our goals. You've got this! [learn more](GST321_U9_T1#GST321_U9_T1_h1)

question: Why is calling anticoagulants 'blood thinners' a bit misleading?

options.A: They do not change the actual thickness or texture of the blood
options.B: They dissolve fat molecules inside the blood vessels instead
options.C: They only affect plasma proteins and leave red blood cells alone
options.D: They actually make the blood thicker while slowing it down

explanation: Even though everyone calls them 'blood thinners,' they don't make your blood watery like juice! They just block specific clotting steps to keep your blood flowing smoothly. [learn more](GNS223_U1_T5#GNS223_U1_T5_h1)

question: How should a nurse handle cultural beliefs that attribute hereditary conditions solely to spiritual curses?

options.A: Publicly ridicule the family for holding traditional beliefs
options.B: Refuse to treat patients who mention spiritual explanations
options.C: Agree with the curse theory to avoid arguing with patients
options.D: Provide gentle, respectful education while addressing community myths

explanation: Nurses can bridge traditional beliefs and medical science through respectful education and community sensitization rather than harsh judgment. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T15#GNS311_U1_T15_h6)

question: What is a common source of emotional stress for school-aged children?

options.A: Academic pressure and peer bullying
options.B: Excessive amounts of physical exercise
options.C: Access to clean drinking water
options.D: Frequent participation in school sports

explanation: Spot on! Hard schoolwork and issues with classmates are major stressors that can weigh heavily on a child's mental health. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T2#GNS225_U4_T2_h7)

question: A patient getting subcutaneous heparin complains of mild skin irritation at the injection site. What should you do?

options.A: Switch the patient to oral aspirin to bypass the skin route
options.B: Stop all future doses of heparin immediately without telling the doctor
options.C: Massage the injection site vigorously to spread the medication faster
options.D: Apply a warm compress and avoid rubbing the site to prevent bruising

explanation: Never massage a heparin injection site! Massaging can burst tiny blood vessels underneath and cause a nasty bruise or hematoma. Just rotate your sites! [learn more](GNS223_U1_T5#GNS223_U1_T5_h6)

question: What is a major root cause of unwanted pregnancies that lead to unsafe abortions?

options.A: Universal access to emergency birth control pills
options.B: Unmet needs and lack of access to modern contraceptives
options.C: Mandatory sex education classes in all primary schools
options.D: Excessive availability of free family planning clinics

explanation: When people cannot get or afford reliable birth control, unplanned pregnancies happen more often. Patient education is our best tool here! [learn more](GNS226_U5_T003#GNS226_U5_T003_h3)

question: Why is the final monitoring and evaluation step so important in the Nutrition Care Process?

options.A: To replace the initial nutrition diagnosis with a new disease
options.B: To bill the hospital insurance company for services rendered
options.C: To discharge the patient immediately from the hospital ward
options.D: To check if the nutritional plan is working and make changes

explanation: Correct! Monitoring lets us see if our dietary plan is actually helping the patient or if we need to switch things up. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T002#GNS227_U4_T002_h5)

question: What is the very first thing a nurse must do if a needle count is incorrect?

options.A: Inform the surgeon and stop wound closure
options.B: Clean up the operating room and send the patient away
options.C: Wait until the patient wakes up to ask if they feel pain
options.D: Write an incident report and leave the theatre

explanation: Brilliant clinical thinking! Never let a wound be closed when a count is wrong. Always speak up right away. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T8#GNS123_U5_T8_h5)

question: The Human Papillomavirus (HPV) vaccine is most famous for helping prevent which major health condition?

options.A: Acquired immunodeficiency syndrome
options.B: Cervical cancer
options.C: Bacterial vaginosis
options.D: Pelvic inflammatory disease

explanation: Correct! The HPV vaccine protects against high-risk strains that can lead to cervical changes and cancer later in life. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T5#GNS216_U5_T5_h4)

question: What is the usual immediate effect of early marriage on a young girl's education?

options.A: It usually forces her to drop out of formal education completely
options.B: It gives her extra time to study advanced university subjects
options.C: It requires her to transfer to a special boarding school for married women
options.D: It has no measurable impact on her daily school attendance

explanation: Correct! Household chores and marital responsibilities almost always cut short a young girl's schooling. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T13#GNS312_U1_T13_h4)

question: Where in the digestive tract do most oral drugs actually get absorbed into the body?

options.A: The small intestine
options.B: The esophagus
options.C: The stomach
options.D: The large intestine

explanation: The small intestine is the champion of absorption! With its massive surface area covered in tiny villi, it's the main highway for drugs to enter the bloodstream. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T4#GNS125_U3_T4_h3)

question: A patient falls ill with typhoid after drinking contaminated water. What type of transmission is this?

options.A: Vector-borne transmission
options.B: Indirect transmission
options.C: Airborne transmission
options.D: Direct transmission

explanation: You got it! Because the water acted as a vehicle between the source and the patient, it counts as indirect transmission. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T1#GNS313_U2_T1_h3)

question: Why is drinking plenty of water especially critical for a nursing mother?

options.A: Lactation permanently increases core body temperature
options.B: Nursing mothers completely stop feeling thirsty
options.C: Milk production requires extra sodium from blood
options.D: Breast milk is composed mostly of water

explanation: Spot on! Since breast milk is mostly water, nursing mums need extra fluids to keep up their milk supply and stay hydrated. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T011#GNS227_U2_T011_h5)

question: What is the primary function of the microscopic microvilli lining the proximal convoluted tubule?

options.A: To increase surface area for reabsorbing substances
options.B: To push urine upward toward the renal cortex
options.C: To trap large red blood cells before filtration
options.D: To secrete excess white blood cells into the filtrate

explanation: Microvilli create a brush border that greatly expands the surface area available to pull water and nutrients back into the blood. [learn more](GNS121_U2_T5#GNS121_U2_T5_h3)

question: Besides published research, what else does evidence-based nursing practice bring together?

options.A: Superstition and historical habits
options.B: Personal intuition and strict tradition
options.C: Clinical expertise and patient preferences
options.D: Hospital budgets and physician seniority

explanation: Good evidence-based practice blends the best research with your own clinical judgment and what matters most to the patient. [learn more](GNS217_U1_T3#GNS217_U1_T3_h8)

question: What is the main goal of injection safety in your daily clinical practice?

options.A: Administering medication without causing harm to patients or yourself
options.B: Using only intravenous routes for fluid replacement
options.C: Ensuring every patient gets at least one daily injection
options.D: Disposing of all used syringes in household trash bins

explanation: You've got this! Injection safety is all about protecting everyone—patients, healthcare workers, and the community—from any harm related to injections. [learn more](GNS122_U4_T2#GNS122_U4_T2_h1)

question: A client with advanced dementia who wanders at night is being checked into an assisted living facility that does not have a secure memory unit. What should the facility do?

options.A: Wait until the client's memory improves on its own
options.B: Deny admission because the facility cannot keep the client safe
options.C: Admit the client and just use door chimes for night safety
options.D: Accept the client and assign a private nurse paid by the family

explanation: You've got this! Facilities must match their care to what the client genuinely needs. Admitting a wandering client to an unsecure place creates a big safety risk. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T6#GNS324_U5_T6_h2)

question: Which of these is NOT a common cause of growth faltering in infants?

options.A: Regular daily physical exercise
options.B: Frequent bouts of childhood diarrhea
options.C: Inadequate complementary feeding
options.D: Recurrent malarial infections

explanation: Normal baby movement doesn't cause faltering. Illness, infections, and poor feeding are the real culprits behind slowed growth. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T55#GNS214_U1_T55_h7)

question: What is the main chart midwives use during labor to track progress and catch problems early?

options.A: Partograph
options.B: Stethoscope
options.C: Sphygmomanometer
options.D: Otoscope

explanation: Correct! The partograph is a simple yet powerful graphical chart that helps us monitor labor and spot when things are taking too long. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T002#GNS226_U1_T002_h4)

question: A nurse is talking to an overweight teenager about healthy eating. What is the most encouraging and effective approach?

options.A: Directly warning the teenager about how bad their body shape looks
options.B: Focusing the discussion on energy, athletic performance, and well-being without shaming
options.C: Ignoring diet completely and focusing only on prescription medication
options.D: Strictly forbidding all favorite foods to force rapid weight loss

explanation: Encouragement wins every time! Focusing on feeling good, having more energy, and performing well works much better than shaming or strict starvation diets. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T007#GNS227_U2_T007_h7)

question: What does a Vaccine Vial Monitor (VVM) tell you?

options.A: The exact number of doses remaining inside the glass vial
options.B: Whether heat exposure has damaged the vaccine's potency
options.C: Whether the vaccine container has been contaminated with bacteria
options.D: The precise manufacturing date printed on the cardboard box

explanation: Think of the VVM as a heat-watchdog! It changes color when exposed to too much heat, letting you know if the vaccine is still safe to use. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T64#GNS214_U1_T64_h3)

question: What is the primary reason a newborn baby born to a diabetic mother often develops hypoglycemia shortly after birth?

options.A: The baby's high insulin production continues after the maternal glucose supply stops
options.B: The baby's liver is completely unable to produce any glycogen stores
options.C: Breast milk contains far too little sugar to nourish a large infant
options.D: The umbilical cord contains insulin-destroying enzymes

explanation: Inside the womb, the baby made extra insulin to handle the mother's high sugar. Once born, that high insulin level keeps working and quickly drops the baby's blood sugar too low. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T006#GNS226_U4_T006_h3)

question: Which physical finding is a classic sign of severe protein deficiency?

options.A: Swollen and painful finger joints
options.B: Yellow discoloration of the eyes
options.C: Extreme sensitivity to sunlight
options.D: Dry, brittle, and easily pluckable hair

explanation: Protein builds hair shafts. When protein is low, hair becomes weak, dry, and pulls out very easily. [learn more](GNS227_U5_T004#GNS227_U5_T004_h4)

question: A patient asks about the tough, fibrous outer sheath covering the erectile tissue of the penis. What is it called?

options.A: Tunica albuginea
options.B: Perineal membrane
options.C: Dartos fascia
options.D: Scrotal septum

explanation: The tunica albuginea is a strong, protective jacket of connective tissue that holds everything firmly in place during an erection. [learn more](GNS121_U4_T1#GNS121_U4_T1_h3)

question: Which of these is NOT a common sign of meningitis?

options.A: High fever and body chills
options.B: Sudden complete paralysis of the lower limbs
options.C: Severe and pounding headache
options.D: Stiff and painful neck movement

explanation: Spot on! Meningitis causes terrible headaches, fever, and a stiff neck, but leg paralysis is not a standard sign of the infection. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T8#GNS211_U3_T8_h7)

question: A patient's blood pressure drops dangerously low after heavy bleeding. Which nursing action shows you are thinking about the whole body?

options.A: Telling the patient that other body organs are completely unaffected
options.B: Focusing solely on applying a bandage to the bleeding wound
options.C: Giving a sleeping pill to help the patient rest through the stress
options.D: Checking urine output because low blood pressure affects kidney function

explanation: Brilliant! Good nursing means remembering that blood loss reduces blood flow to vital organs like the kidneys, which immediately shows up in their urine output. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T9#GNS111_U1_T9_h5)

question: You notice a fellow nurse showing signs of severe impairment while on duty. What is the best professional step to take?

options.A: Keep the secret permanently and let the impaired nurse handle critical drug doses alone
options.B: Report the observation safely through institutional channels to protect patients and help the colleague
options.C: Steal some of the leftover medications for personal use after the shift ends
options.D: Shout insults at the colleague in front of patients and visitors in the hallway

explanation: Patient safety always comes first, but we also want to guide our struggling colleagues toward the help they need through proper, confidential channels. [learn more](GNS125_U4_T3#GNS125_U4_T3_h8)

question: What do we call the ongoing health issues that linger for months after recovering from initial COVID-19?

options.A: Post-infectious immunity
options.B: Secondary sepsis
options.C: Acute viral syndrome
options.D: Long COVID

explanation: Correct! 'Long COVID' is the term used when symptoms stick around long after the acute virus has cleared the body. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T6#GNS123_U4_T6_h8)

question: What is the main goal of the intensive phase of TB treatment?

options.A: To test if the patient is allergic to all four drugs
options.B: To rapidly reduce the bacterial load and stop infectiousness
options.C: To rebuild the damaged lung tissue back to normal
options.D: To completely finish the entire course of treatment

explanation: Hitting TB hard with four drugs quickly drops the germ count so the patient stops spreading it to others. Excellent clinical milestone! [learn more](GNS223_U2_T6#GNS223_U2_T6_h4)

question: A patient with a new leg cast says their toes feel very numb and tingly. What should the nurse do first?

options.A: Perform a complete neurovascular assessment and report findings
options.B: Massage the toes gently to restore normal local blood circulation
options.C: Elevate the leg above heart level and encourage deep breathing
options.D: Administer a prescribed oral sleeping pill to calm the patient

explanation: Numbness and tingling are red flags for trapped nerves or poor blood flow. Checking thoroughly and reporting right away keeps the patient safe. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T11#GNS324_U4_T11_h3)

question: Why is it best to look for local strengths in the community before asking for outside donations?

options.A: External organizations refuse to work with community nurses
options.B: Local materials are always completely free of charge
options.C: Outside donors are legally banned from helping health clinics
options.D: It builds self-reliance so the program can keep running long-term

explanation: Spot on! Using local assets empowers the community so the project doesn't collapse the moment outside help stops. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T19#GNS225_U2_T19_h6)

question: Why must a working defibrillator be kept close by during an EPS?

options.A: Dangerous heart rhythms are purposely triggered during the test
options.B: Sedation medications frequently cause permanent heart stoppage
options.C: The equipment is required to warm up the contrast dye
options.D: All patients suffer sudden cardiac arrest during catheter insertion

explanation: Because the doctors intentionally spark those weird rhythms to study them, the team must always be ready with a defibrillator just in case the heart needs help getting back to normal. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T10#GNS222_U3_T10_h4)

question: How does a well-motivated nurse protect patient safety at the bedside?

options.A: By removing the need for doctors to write formal medication orders
options.B: By automatically doubling the nurse-to-patient staffing ratio
options.C: By increasing vigilance to catch subtle signs of clinical deterioration early
options.D: By speeding up the discharge process regardless of clinical status

explanation: When you are alert and motivated, you easily notice tiny changes in a patient's condition and can save the day early! [learn more](GST321_U3_T7#GST321_U3_T7_h4)

question: A clinic makes sure patients from all backgrounds receive the exact same high standard of treatment. Which quality dimension is this?

options.A: Equity
options.B: Efficiency
options.C: Timeliness
options.D: Effectiveness

explanation: Well done! Equity means fairness—ensuring every patient gets great, high-quality care regardless of their background, status, or wealth. [learn more](GST319_U2_T1#GST319_U2_T1_h2)

question: Which food choice is generally NOT recommended when mixing crushed medication for an infant?

options.A: A small taste of flavored pudding
options.B: A spoonful of sweet applesauce
options.C: Daily milk or formula bottle feeds
options.D: A small drop of fruit puree

explanation: Mixing drugs into routine milk feeds can cause the infant to reject their primary nutrition if the taste changes. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T14#GNS122_U1_T14_h6)

question: What is the main job of flat bones in the body?

options.A: Absorbing high impact forces in tight spaces like the wrist
options.B: Acting as long levers to propel the body forward during running
options.C: Guiding tendons smoothly across major joints without friction
options.D: Protecting internal organs and providing broad muscle attachment sites

explanation: Flat bones (like your skull and sternum) act like helmets and shields for vital organs while giving muscles a wide place to anchor. [learn more](GNS121_U3_T4#GNS121_U3_T4_h4)

question: How can you make sure your midwifery kit is always ready for an emergency call?

options.A: By washing the outside canvas bag once a year
options.B: By keeping the bag tightly locked until an emergency happens
options.C: By swapping metal tools for plastic toys to stay light
options.D: By checking inventory and expiry dates after every single use

explanation: Restocking and checking dates right after a case means you will never open your bag during an emergency only to find something expired or missing! [learn more](GNS225_U3_T10#GNS225_U3_T10_h8)

question: Which quick test is most commonly used at the bedside to check for a collapsed lung?

options.A: Chest X-ray
options.B: Magnetic resonance imaging
options.C: Pulmonary function testing
options.D: Bronchoscopy

explanation: A quick chest X-ray gives us an immediate picture of what's going on inside the chest cavity. Keep up the great diagnostic thinking! [learn more](GNS213_U2_T7#GNS213_U2_T7_h4)

question: What is a single nucleotide polymorphism, often called an SNP?

options.A: A chemical bond connecting two different proteins
options.B: An extra chromosome found in inherited disorders
options.C: A tiny alteration in a single building block of DNA
options.D: A complete deletion of an entire human gene

explanation: Great job! An SNP is simply a common, tiny variation where just one building block in the DNA sequence differs from person to person. [learn more](GNS125_U1_T5#GNS125_U1_T5_h2)

question: Why must you perform a bimanual pelvic exam before putting in an IUD?

options.A: To confirm the client is definitely not ovulating
options.B: To stretch the cervix open without using instruments
options.C: To check the weight of the client's ovaries
options.D: To check the size and position of the uterus

explanation: Feeling the uterus first helps you know its exact angle and size so you can insert the device safely without accidentally poking through the uterine wall. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T015#GNS226_U6_T015_h4)

question: What does the letter 'I' stand for in the DESC communication script?

options.A: Ignore the doctor
options.B: Inspect the patient
options.C: Express your feeling
options.D: Initiate treatment

explanation: In the DESC script, E stands for Expressing how the situation affects you or the patient. [learn more](GST321_U7_T5#GST321_U7_T5_h5)

question: What does giving 'holistic nursing care' mean?

options.A: Exclusively treating the biological cause of the acute disease
options.B: The physical, emotional, social, and spiritual dimensions of the client
options.C: Strictly checking the financial cost of prescribed drugs
options.D: Only looking at physical lab test results on the chart

explanation: Fantastic! Holistic care means treating the whole person—body, mind, emotions, and spirit, not just a disease. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T3#GNS112_U2_T3_h8)

question: A study compares a new diet to standard care for weight loss and finds p = 0.001. What should a nurse take away from this?

options.A: The diet has no clinical value whatsoever
options.B: The weight loss difference is statistically significant
options.C: All patients lost the exact same amount of weight
options.D: The study had a major error in data collection

explanation: A tiny p-value like 0.001 is way below 0.05, which gives us strong statistical confidence that the diet made a real difference. [learn more](GNS217_U4_T14#GNS217_U4_T14_h7)

question: Why is the partograph considered such a helpful early warning tool in the labour room?

options.A: It automatically orders emergency caesarean sections from the pharmacy
options.B: It alerts staff to deviations from normal labour before complications become severe
options.C: It predicts the exact gender and birth weight of the baby days in advance
options.D: It rings an electronic alarm bell whenever a contraction starts

explanation: Spotting small changes early makes all the difference. By plotting readings over time, you can catch slow progress or distress early and step in to help. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T007#GNS226_U3_T007_h1)

question: Which specific vitamin needs a special helper protein called 'intrinsic factor' from the stomach to be absorbed properly?

options.A: Folic acid
options.B: Vitamin B12
options.C: Vitamin K
options.D: Vitamin C

explanation: Intrinsic factor is like a VIP escort for Vitamin B12! It teams up in the stomach to protect the vitamin until they reach the lower part of the small intestine for absorption. [learn more](GNS121_U1_T7#GNS121_U1_T7_h5)

question: Which layer of the outer adrenal gland (adrenal cortex) produces stress hormones like cortisol?

options.A: Zona glomerulosa
options.B: Zona reticularis
options.C: Adrenal medulla
options.D: Zona fasciculata

explanation: Think of the adrenal cortex layers from outside in as Salt, Sugar, Sex (Glomerulosa, Fasciculata, Reticularis). The middle layer, zona fasciculata, handles the 'sugar' hormones like cortisol to help you cope with stress! [learn more](GNS211_U1_T2#GNS211_U1_T2_h4)

question: Which classic body sign gives yellow fever its name?

options.A: Cyanosis
options.B: Jaundice
options.C: Erythema
options.D: Pallor

explanation: Exactly! Liver trouble causes jaundice—a yellowing of the skin and eyes—which inspired the illness's name. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T9#GNS214_U1_T9_h4)

question: What is the main focus of quantitative research?

options.A: Historical observation of ancient medical texts
options.B: Open-ended interviews about emotional trauma
options.C: Numerical measurement and statistical analysis
options.D: Detailed personal stories of patient suffering

explanation: Quantitative research is all about numbers, counting, and statistics. If you can measure it, it's quantitative! [learn more](GNS224_U1_T6#GNS224_U1_T6_h2)

question: Which of the following is NOT one of the essential clean delivery practices?

options.A: Clean cutting instrument for the cord
options.B: Clean surgical face mask for every visitor
options.C: Clean surface for the mother to deliver on
options.D: Clean hands of the birth attendant

explanation: The core clean delivery practices focus on hands, delivery surface, perineum, cord cutting tools, and cord ties rather than visitor masks. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T50#GNS214_U1_T50_h6)

question: A hypertensive patient keeps missing clinic days and stopped taking their drugs. As their nurse, what is your best next step?

options.A: Assume the patient is completely cured and stop calling their phone number
options.B: Conduct a home visit to discuss barriers to compliance and provide tailored education
options.C: Discharge the patient permanently from the clinic registry without further discussion
options.D: Report the patient to local law enforcement authorities for policy violation

explanation: Wonderful nursing judgment! Visiting them helps you find out why they stopped—maybe money is tight or side effects are bothering them—so you can help find a solution together. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T1#GNS313_U3_T1_h6)

question: Why is it important to suction the back of the throat right before removing an endotracheal tube?

options.A: To make it easier to deflate the inner balloon cuff
options.B: To test whether the patient's gag reflex is fully recovered
options.C: To prevent pooling secretions from sliding down into the lungs
options.D: To measure the exact amount of saliva produced during sleep

explanation: Suctioning above the cuff clears out collected saliva and mucus so they do not get aspirated into the trachea as the tube comes out. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T16#GNS213_U2_T16_h8)

question: A pregnant woman in a remote village starts bleeding heavily during labor. What is the most critical factor that decides if she survives?

options.A: The weather forecast for the upcoming week
options.B: Whether she ate a balanced diet during her first trimester
options.C: Her family's ability to buy infant clothing ahead of time
options.D: Quick transport to a facility with emergency obstetric care

explanation: In emergencies like severe bleeding, every minute counts! Getting the mother quickly to a hospital that can handle obstetric emergencies is often the difference between life and death. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T4#GNS216_U1_T4_h2)

question: When trying to keep people safe from chemicals at work, what is considered the absolute best first step?

options.A: Conducting weekly medical tests on every worker
options.B: Handing out expensive protective gear to all staff
options.C: Putting warning signs on every single office door
options.D: Replacing a toxic chemical with a safer alternative

explanation: Brilliant! Substituting a dangerous chemical with a safer one completely removes the hazard instead of just managing the risk. Elimination is always the gold standard in safety. [learn more](GNS215_U5_T8#GNS215_U5_T8_h3)

question: When does intrapartum transmission of HIV primarily take place?

options.A: Through breast milk during the first week of life
options.B: As the baby passes through the birth canal
options.C: Across the placenta during the first trimester
options.D: Via airborne droplets in the delivery room

explanation: Intrapartum transmission happens when the infant is exposed to infected maternal blood and vaginal fluids during labor and birth. [learn more](GNS216_U6_T11#GNS216_U6_T11_h2)

question: Which of these details is typically recorded in the stock inventory part of the safety form?

options.A: The personal home address of every patient
options.B: Opening balance and quantities used
options.C: Detailed medical diagnoses of injection recipients
options.D: Daily weather conditions at the facility

explanation: Correct! The stock section is strictly about numbers: what we started with, what we used, and what is left. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T11#GNS122_U3_T11_h3)

question: What is the normal range for intracranial pressure in adults?

options.A: 30 to 50 mmHg
options.B: 80 to 120 mmHg
options.C: 120 to 160 mmHg
options.D: 5 to 15 mmHg

explanation: Normal ICP is low, ranging between 5 and 15 mmHg. Anything persistently higher requires immediate medical and nursing intervention. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T21#GNS222_U3_T21_h4)

question: Imagine you almost give an oral syrup through an intravenous (IV) line by mistake. Which medication right did you almost break?

options.A: Right Documentation
options.B: Right Route
options.C: Right Dose
options.D: Right Time

explanation: The 'Right Route' means giving the drug through the exact pathway the doctor ordered (like oral versus IV). Always double-check how the drug is supposed to enter the body! [learn more](GNS125_U4_T1#GNS125_U4_T1_h2)

question: A newborn is scheduled for circumcision, but you notice the urethral opening is on the underside of the penis. What should you do?

options.A: Report the finding and hold the procedure because the foreskin may be needed for future repair
options.B: Apply an antiseptic ointment and wrap the penis tightly in gauze
options.C: Proceed with the circumcision quickly before the doctor arrives
options.D: Reassure the mother that this is a normal variation

explanation: This condition is called hypospadias. Always hold off on circumcision and report it—surgeons actually need that extra foreskin tissue to reconstruct the urethra later! [learn more](GNS311_U4_T5#GNS311_U4_T5_h3)

question: What is the very first thing a health worker must do during community entry?

options.A: Immunize all children under five years old
options.B: Build a modern primary health care clinic
options.C: Conduct a random drug trial in the village
options.D: Gain permission from traditional rulers and gatekeepers

explanation: Respecting local leadership through formal entry and greeting gatekeepers builds trust and opens doors for the healthcare team. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T5#GNS124_U4_T5_h2)

question: What is the main goal of food fortification programs in public health?

options.A: Removing harmful chemical additives from local markets
options.B: Extending the shelf life of perishable meats
options.C: Adding essential nutrients to everyday foods to protect populations
options.D: Lowering the market cost of imported luxury foods

explanation: You got it! Fortifying common foods like salt or flour ensures that whole communities get key nutrients like iron and iodine without changing their daily habits. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T13#GNS313_U2_T13_h5)

question: Which of these conditions is a major reason to put a patient on a low-sodium diet?

options.A: Iron deficiency anemia
options.B: Type 1 diabetes mellitus
options.C: Chronic bone fractures
options.D: Congestive heart failure

explanation: Well done! Heart failure patients can't handle extra fluid volume, so keeping salt low helps protect their lungs and heart. [learn more](GNS227_U6_T008#GNS227_U6_T008_h3)

question: What should you do if a patient cannot remember the names of their home medications?

options.A: Disregard home drugs and start fresh hospital drugs
options.B: Guess the medications based on their visible disease symptoms
options.C: Scold the patient for being careless with their health
options.D: Ask the patient or family to bring all medicine containers to the clinic

explanation: Having them bring their actual bottles or sachets gives you exact, reliable data when memory fails. Simple and practical! [learn more](GNS215_U2_T2#GNS215_U2_T2_h4)

question: What is usually the most important factor in keeping a synovial joint stable?

options.A: Length of the bones
options.B: Thickness of the skin
options.C: Muscle tone
options.D: Amount of synovial fluid

explanation: Well done! The constant, healthy tension in the muscles surrounding a joint (muscle tone) is what keeps everything safely in place. [learn more](GNS121_U3_T5#GNS121_U3_T5_h7)

question: A patient is brought to the ward in a deep coma after a severe head injury. Which nursing action is best to prevent stiff joints?

options.A: Doing regular passive range of motion exercises
options.B: Encouraging the client to squeeze rubber balls daily
options.C: Tying all four limbs tightly to the bed rails
options.D: Putting heavy sandbags on the hands and feet

explanation: Brilliant! An unconscious client cannot move on their own, so scheduled passive range of motion keeps their joints mobile and safe. [learn more](GNS221_U1_T3#GNS221_U1_T3_h2)

question: A nurse uses self-awareness to connect authentically with a frightened patient. Which pattern of knowing is this?

options.A: Personal knowing
options.B: Empirical knowing
options.C: Aesthetic knowing
options.D: Ethical knowing

explanation: Personal knowing is about looking inward and using self-reflection to build a genuine, trusting relationship with your patient. [learn more](GNS217_U1_T2#GNS217_U1_T2_h2)

question: What was the main focus of nursing studies during the early part of the twentieth century?

options.A: Hospital staffing and nursing education
options.B: Molecular genetics and cellular biology
options.C: Pharmacological drug trials
options.D: Advanced surgical techniques

explanation: Early research mostly looked at how to organize nursing schools, manage hospital routines, and assign student workloads efficiently. [learn more](GNS217_U2_T3#GNS217_U2_T3_h2)

question: What is the main goal of the Essential Drug Programme in public health?

options.A: Ensuring safe and affordable medicines are always available
options.B: Eliminating the need for doctors in rural clinics
options.C: Reducing the overall salaries of hospital pharmacy staff
options.D: Promoting only foreign-manufactured pharmaceutical brands

explanation: You got this! The whole point of the Essential Drug Programme is to make sure vital, quality medicines remain easy to get and affordable for everyone. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T6#GNS215_U1_T6_h1)

question: What is the best eating strategy for a patient dealing with severe nausea and poor appetite?

options.A: Encouraging three large, heavy meals to catch up on lost calories
options.B: Forcing the patient to finish everything on a large dinner plate
options.C: Withholding all food until appetite returns spontaneously
options.D: Serving small, frequent nutrient-dense meals throughout the day

explanation: Huge meals can make a nauseous patient feel worse. Small, tasty bites spaced through the day are much easier to manage! [learn more](GNS321_U1_T11#GNS321_U1_T11_h7)

question: In the early days following Nightingale's work, what was the main focus of nursing studies?

options.A: Advanced surgical interventions
options.B: Pharmaceutical drug development
options.C: Hospital financial management
options.D: Nursing education and training methods

explanation: Spot on! Before diving heavily into clinical care, early nurse researchers first wanted to figure out the best ways to train and educate nurses. [learn more](GNS217_U2_T4#GNS217_U2_T4_h2)

question: How can taking unregulated herbal remedies during pregnancy lead to birth defects?

options.A: They cause an immediate miscarriage without touching fetal structure
options.B: They may contain teratogens that disrupt baby's organ formation
options.C: They speed up the growth of the placenta too quickly
options.D: They permanently lower the mother's blood pressure

explanation: Substances that mess with normal development are called teratogens. Many local herbal mixes haven't been safety-tested for pregnancy, so it's always safer to stick to prescribed antenatal vitamins! [learn more](GNS226_U3_T020#GNS226_U3_T020_h2)

question: Which pain scale uses cartoon faces ranging from a happy smile to a crying face?

options.A: Behavioral Pain Scale
options.B: Visual Analog Scale
options.C: Wong-Baker FACES Scale
options.D: Numeric Rating Scale

explanation: The Wong-Baker FACES scale uses friendly facial drawings, making it super helpful for children or patients who struggle to use numbers. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T5#GNS321_U4_T5_h4)

question: What makes postpartum hemorrhage (PPH) such a major emergency for a new mother?

options.A: Chronic infection of the urinary tract
options.B: Severe blood loss that can quickly cause death
options.C: Permanent paralysis of the lower limbs
options.D: Sudden permanent loss of vision

explanation: Exactly. Postpartum hemorrhage means rapid, heavy bleeding after birth. If we don't replace the blood volume quickly, it can lead to severe shock and danger very fast. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T014#GNS226_U1_T014_h2)

question: What does the term ACE stand for when studying childhood and mental health?

options.A: Acute Clinical Evaluation
options.B: Adverse Childhood Experiences
options.C: Affective Coping Environment
options.D: Anxiety and Crisis Education

explanation: ACE stands for Adverse Childhood Experiences—tough or traumatic events that happen before a person turns eighteen. [learn more](GNS314_U4_T1#GNS314_U4_T1_h4)

question: Which symptom is a classic presentation of cervical friability in cervicitis?

options.A: Complete cessation of menses
options.B: Inability to control urination
options.C: Postcoital bleeding
options.D: Severe lower back stiffness

explanation: Because inflamed cervical tissue is very fragile, contact during sexual intercourse frequently causes postcoital spotting or bleeding. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T14#GNS216_U5_T14_h4)

question: Why must bed sheets in a hospital stay completely free of wrinkles?

options.A: Wrinkles make it difficult for the patient to adjust their pillows
options.B: Wrinkles signal to visitors that the nursing staff is careless
options.C: Wrinkles trap trapped air and cause the room temperature to rise
options.D: Wrinkles increase friction and pressure on the skin, leading to sores

explanation: You got it! Smooth sheets protect your patient's skin by preventing friction and pressure points that cause painful bedsores. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T3#GNS112_U4_T3_h1)

question: A nurse manager suddenly sees patient admissions double overnight. Which budgeting phase does this affect the most?

options.A: Historical auditing of past years
options.B: Initial executive board selection
options.C: Implementation and monitoring
options.D: Capital equipment depreciation

explanation: This happens during the live implementation phase, where managers constantly watch real-time patient numbers and adjust on the fly! [learn more](GST321_U1_T24#GST321_U1_T24_h3)

question: Which chemical messengers travel to the brain to raise body temperature and cause a fever during an infection?

options.A: Antibodies
options.B: Platelets
options.C: Histamines
options.D: Pyrogens

explanation: You got it! Pyrogens act like the body's internal thermostat adjusters, signaling the brain to turn up the heat to fight off invaders. [learn more](GST114_U2_T4#GST114_U2_T4_h2)

question: Which landmark sits right between the front and back fontanelles on a baby's head?

options.A: The mentum
options.B: The vertex
options.C: The base
options.D: The face

explanation: You've got this! The vertex is simply the top part of the head, located right between the two main soft spots (fontanelles). [learn more](GNS121_U6_T13#GNS121_U6_T13_h1)

question: What should the nurse do immediately after using an instrument during a home visit?

options.A: Return it straight into the clean section of the bag
options.B: Give it to the family members to wash later
options.C: Place it on the bare floor next to the patient's bed
options.D: Keep it separated and clean it before storing it away

explanation: Used equipment must never mix with clean supplies and requires proper cleaning and disinfection before going back into the bag. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T11#GNS225_U2_T11_h3)

question: Why is proper healthcare waste management considered a key infection control practice?

options.A: It prevents the spread of harmful microorganisms found in discarded items
options.B: It speeds up the process of discharging stable patients from the ward
options.C: It lowers the monthly electricity and water utility bills of the facility
options.D: It ensures the hospital compounds look neat and presentable to visitors

explanation: Spot on! Discarded medical materials often carry germs that can multiply and spread infections if we don't handle them right. You're doing great! [learn more](GST114_U6_T5#GST114_U6_T5_h1)

question: Why do we bother grouping drugs into different classes?

options.A: To eliminate the need for nurses to check patient vital signs
options.B: To dictate the exact financial cost of each medication in the pharmacy
options.C: To ensure that every drug has exactly one trade name worldwide
options.D: To group medications with similar properties and manage vast pharmaceutical knowledge

explanation: You're right on track! There are thousands of drugs out there, and classification helps us make sense of them by grouping similar ones together. [learn more](GNS125_U1_T3#GNS125_U1_T3_h4)

question: Who represents a multidisciplinary team working together in a rural community setting?

options.A: Individual nurses working in complete isolation from peers
options.B: Only senior hospital physicians meeting in private offices
options.C: A group of patients waiting outside a closed pharmacy
options.D: Nurses, environmental health officers, and social workers

explanation: You've got this! Healthcare isn't a one-person show. Bringing nurses, sanitation officers, and social workers together ensures we tackle health problems from every angle. [learn more](GNS225_U1_T9#GNS225_U1_T9_h5)

question: Which of these actions is WRONG when caring for a patient with a known severe drug allergy?

options.A: Telling the patient they can safely take a tiny dose of the drug again
options.B: Putting clear allergy alerts in the patient chart
options.C: Notifying the hospital pharmacy about the allergy
options.D: Educating the family on how to avoid the drug

explanation: Never give a drug again if a patient has a true severe allergy! They must avoid it completely for life. [learn more](GNS215_U5_T4#GNS215_U5_T4_h8)

question: What is a main reason why women struggle to pass urine during or right after childbirth?

options.A: High concentration of glucose in the urine
options.B: Pressure of the foetal head on the bladder neck
options.C: Sudden complete shutdown of the glomeruli
options.D: Severe dehydration caused by hyperemesis

explanation: As the baby moves down the birth canal, the head can temporarily press on and block the urethra, making it hard to empty the bladder. Totally normal to encounter in labor wards! [learn more](GNS121_U7_T5#GNS121_U7_T5_h4)

question: Which level of healthcare prevention includes traditional rehabilitation activities?

options.A: Secondary prevention
options.B: Quaternary prevention
options.C: Primary prevention
options.D: Tertiary prevention

explanation: Tertiary prevention is all about managing existing long-term issues, preventing complications, and getting the patient to their highest possible function. [learn more](GNS123_U6_T1#GNS123_U6_T1_h5)

question: What naturally happens to the outer layer of the skin as a person ages?

options.A: It becomes thinner and loses its elasticity
options.B: It produces significantly more sweat and oil
options.C: It permanently changes its original pigmentation
options.D: It grows thicker and develops more fat layers

explanation: As we age, our skin loses collagen and the epidermis gets thinner. This makes older adults' skin much more fragile and prone to tears or bruises. Good to keep in mind during daily care! [learn more](GNS324_U3_T2#GNS324_U3_T2_h2)

question: How does poor, slumped posture affect a patient's breathing?

options.A: It stops the movement of the diaphragm completely
options.B: It increases the total volume of air the lungs can hold
options.C: It causes rapid overinflation of the chest cavity
options.D: It restricts lung expansion and reduces oxygen intake

explanation: Slumping scrunches up the chest cavity, leaving the lungs with very little room to stretch out and take in a deep, refreshing breath. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T5#GNS112_U4_T5_h3)

question: Which hormone directly builds up and thickens the uterine lining during the first half of the cycle?

options.A: Prolactin
options.B: Oxytocin
options.C: Estrogen
options.D: Progesterone

explanation: Think of estrogen as the builder hormone! Produced by the growing follicles, it helps rebuild and thicken the endometrium after a period ends. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T4#GNS121_U5_T4_h4)

question: When is compromising a better choice than collaborating?

options.A: When unlimited time is available for deep discussion
options.B: When time is limited and a quick middle ground is needed
options.C: When patient safety is directly and immediately threatened
options.D: When neither party cares about the final outcome

explanation: When you are rushed on the ward and don't have hours to talk things through, splitting the difference (compromising) is a fast, practical fix. [learn more](GST321_U5_T4#GST321_U5_T4_h4)

question: A patient is due for digoxin, but their pulse is 52 beats per minute. What should you do?

options.A: Crush the tablet to speed up its absorption in the stomach
options.B: Hold the medication and notify the prescribing physician
options.C: Give half the dose now and the other half later in the day
options.D: Administer the medication with a glass of orange juice

explanation: Great clinical instinct! Digoxin slows the heart down, so a pulse below 60 means it's safer to hold the drug and call the doctor. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T1#GNS122_U1_T1_h2)

question: A patient has poor wound healing and muscle wasting because they aren't eating enough. What is this called?

options.A: Undernutrition
options.B: Energy balance
options.C: Overnutrition
options.D: Anabolism

explanation: When nutrient intake falls short of what the body needs, it leads to undernutrition, causing issues like muscle wasting and delayed healing. [learn more](GNS227_U1_T001#GNS227_U1_T001_h8)

question: Why is allowing periods of silence during a palliative nursing conversation beneficial?

options.A: It forces the patient to speak up faster
options.B: It gives the patient time to gather thoughts and process heavy emotions
options.C: It allows the nurse to complete charting without talking
options.D: It shows the nurse has run out of medical information to share

explanation: Silence creates a safe, unhurried space for vulnerable patients to process profound thoughts and feelings. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T16#GNS321_U4_T16_h5)

question: Why must Nigerian nurses always check the NAFDAC number on drug packaging?

options.A: To calculate the precise half-life of the drug in the patient's bloodstream
options.B: To find out which pharmaceutical company holds the international trade patent
options.C: To confirm the product is legally approved and guard against fake or substandard drugs
options.D: To determine the exact chemical formula of the active ingredient

explanation: Spot on! Checking for that NAFDAC number is a crucial shield against fake or unsafe medications in clinical practice. [learn more](GNS125_U1_T3#GNS125_U1_T3_h6)

question: Which of these is considered a direct cost of a physical disability?

options.A: Losing daily wages while resting
options.B: Missing a promotion due to bias
options.C: Reduced workplace productivity
options.D: Buying a wheelchair and mobility braces

explanation: Direct costs are the actual out-of-pocket prices you pay for items specifically needed because of the impairment, like assistive devices and drugs. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T12#GNS225_U5_T12_h3)

question: Why are accurate meeting minutes considered important legal records in healthcare?

options.A: They serve as proof of staff attendance for annual salary increases
options.B: They provide a clear audit trail of accountability and quality improvement decisions
options.C: They act as marketing material for prospective nursing students
options.D: They replace the need for patient clinical chart documentation

explanation: Minutes show that the facility actively addressed safety and operational issues over time. [learn more](GST321_U7_T4#GST321_U7_T4_h5)

question: A woman with severe bleeding after childbirth dies because the clinic has no blood and no ambulance to transfer her. Which delay caused this?

options.A: Zero delay
options.B: Third delay
options.C: Second delay
options.D: First delay

explanation: The third delay happens right inside the health facility when care is delayed or inadequate because of shortages in supplies, equipment, or trained staff. You're doing great learning these concepts! [learn more](GNS226_U1_T015#GNS226_U1_T015_h6)

question: What is the main purpose of conducting a physical stock audit on a hospital ward?

options.A: To test the clinical skills of newly employed nurses
options.B: To compare actual items on the shelf with recorded inventory
options.C: To clean out the dust from the medication store cupboards
options.D: To dispose of all old equipment regardless of expiry date

explanation: Stock audits involve counting what is physically present to match it with what the logbook says should be there. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T19#GNS122_U3_T19_h6)

question: How does social stigma make the problem of unsafe abortions even worse?

options.A: It forces women to hide their condition and delay seeking safe help
options.B: It prevents healthcare workers from learning basic nursing skills
options.C: It causes severe hormonal imbalances that mimic pregnancy complications
options.D: It directly reduces the availability of surgical equipment in hospitals

explanation: Spot on. Fear of judgment and shame makes patients wait too long or use dangerous home remedies instead of coming to us for safe care. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T004#GNS226_U5_T004_h2)

question: What does providing integrated services mean in an adolescent clinic?

options.A: Requiring both parents to attend every medical consultation with the teen
options.B: Using traditional medicine alongside modern pharmaceutical drugs
options.C: Offering multiple health services like reproductive and mental care under one roof
options.D: Combining adult and adolescent patients in the same waiting room

explanation: Integrated services mean a young person can access different types of healthcare in a single convenient location. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T16#GNS312_U3_T16_h5)

question: What is the core philosophy of family-centered care in pediatrics?

options.A: Viewing the family as an essential partner in the child's healthcare
options.B: Focusing exclusively on hospital-based procedures
options.C: Excluding family members from daily medical decisions
options.D: Treating the child without input from the parents

explanation: Family-centered care builds on the strengths of families and honors their central role in the child's life. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T6#GNS225_U5_T6_h7)

question: A patient recovering from a large surgical wound requires tissue repair. Which macronutrient should the nurse ensure is adequately provided?

options.A: Carbohydrates
options.B: Fats
options.C: Proteins
options.D: Water

explanation: Proteins supply the amino acids required to build new tissue and heal surgical wounds effectively. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T015#GNS227_U2_T015_h2)

question: What is the main focus of long-term care compared to acute care?

options.A: Performing emergency procedures and trauma resuscitation
options.B: Providing short-term surgical recovery and rapid discharge
options.C: Maintaining quality of life and managing chronic conditions
options.D: Curing acute infections and stabilizing vital signs

explanation: You've got this! While acute care focuses on sudden illnesses, long-term care is all about steady, ongoing support and helping people live well with long-standing health challenges. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T2#GNS324_U5_T2_h1)

question: A lecturer leaves an anatomical chart displayed on the board long after the topic has changed to nursing ethics. What mistake has the lecturer made?

options.A: Poor timing and management of visual distraction
options.B: Failing to check the cost of the material
options.C: Using an inaccurate scientific model
options.D: Selecting a non-projected visual aid

explanation: Leaving media displayed after the discussion has moved on distracts learners and dilutes the focus of the current lesson. [learn more](GST321_U8_T4#GST321_U8_T4_h5)

question: Which of these is NOT a good strategy for teaching a patient with an endocrine condition?

options.A: Providing clear written action plans for emergency symptoms
options.B: Tailoring the teaching session to the patient's cultural background
options.C: Giving long medical lectures without checking for understanding
options.D: Using a return-demonstration approach for practical skills

explanation: Correct! Long, boring lectures don't help anyone learn. We always want interactive teaching and plenty of feedback! [learn more](GNS222_U2_T17#GNS222_U2_T17_h5)

question: What is the very first thing you do right after pulling the needle out of a patient?

options.A: Activate the needle safety device and drop it into a sharps container
options.B: Recap the needle immediately using both hands for safety
options.C: Massage the injection site vigorously to speed up absorption
options.D: Wipe the skin again with a fresh alcohol swab to clean any blood

explanation: Safety first! Always pop the safety on and drop the used needle straight into the sharps box to protect yourself and others from accidental pricks. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T7#GNS125_U3_T7_h5)

question: How do healthcare workers usually trigger artificial active immunity in patients?

options.A: Through an emergency transfusion of donor plasma
options.B: Through the natural recovery from a severe bacterial illness
options.C: Through the application of topical antiseptic ointments
options.D: Through vaccination with weakened or killed antigens

explanation: Vaccines give your immune system a safe preview of a germ (using harmless or dead pieces), tricking it into building up long-term defense memory without getting you sick. [learn more](GST114_U4_T6#GST114_U4_T6_h4)

question: Which mineral salt makes up the hard inorganic part of bone matrix?

options.A: Sodium chloride
options.B: Potassium sulfate
options.C: Calcium phosphate
options.D: Magnesium carbonate

explanation: Calcium phosphate crystals combine with other minerals to form hydroxyapatite, giving bone its hard, rigid quality. [learn more](GNS121_U3_T2#GNS121_U3_T2_h4)

question: What is a very common trigger for dangerous autonomic dysreflexia in a patient with a spinal cord injury?

options.A: Listening to loud music
options.B: Yawning repeatedly in a quiet room
options.C: A full bladder or constipation
options.D: Eating a cold meal too quickly

explanation: Anything irritating the body below the injury level—like a desperately full bladder or trapped stool—can send the nervous system into a dangerous spike called autonomic dysreflexia. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T20#GNS222_U3_T20_h8)

question: During a pelvic exam, what physical sign would you expect in a patient with Type II FGM?

options.A: A completely sealed vaginal opening with a tiny pinhole
options.B: An intact hymen with no external scars
options.C: Extensive scar tissue and absence of the labia minora
options.D: Enlarged, hypertrophied Bartholin glands

explanation: Well done! The removal of both the clitoris and labia minora leaves clear signs of scar tissue and missing external structures. [learn more](GNS225_U6_T2#GNS225_U6_T2_h4)

question: Why does severe liver disease (cirrhosis) often lead to higher levels of active oral drugs in the bloodstream?

options.A: Reduced liver metabolism bypasses normal first-pass breakdown
options.B: The damaged liver absorbs extra medication directly from meals
options.C: Heart output speeds up to push drugs past the liver faster
options.D: Cirrhosis increases the production of helpful blood proteins

explanation: Normally, the liver acts as a checkpoint for oral drugs (first-pass metabolism). If the liver is scarred or failing, it fails to break down its usual share, sending a flood of active drug straight into circulation. [learn more](GNS125_U5_T10#GNS125_U5_T10_h5)

question: What is the typical pH range of fasting gastric juice in a healthy stomach?
explanation: A healthy fasting stomach is strongly acidic, reflected by a low pH reading between 1.5 and 3.5. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T3#GNS213_U3_T3_h5)

question: In traditional Nigerian society, who has mainly taken care of older adults needing support?

options.A: Government-run hospitals
options.B: Non-profit religious charities
options.C: Extended family networks
options.D: Private nursing homes

explanation: You got this! Culturally, our extended family system has always been the primary safety net for caring for our aging loved ones. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T1#GNS324_U5_T1_h1)

question: Why must you remove a medication patch from a patient's chest before putting on AED pads?

options.A: The medication will instantly enter the machine and break the processor.
options.B: The patch makes the skin too slippery for the rescuer to press hard.
options.C: The patch will absorb the conductive gel and ruin the AED pads.
options.D: The patch can block the electrical current and cause skin burns.

explanation: Medication patches can interfere with the electricity and even cause nasty skin burns. Always peel them off and wipe the skin clean first! [learn more](GNS212_U4_T13#GNS212_U4_T13_h5)

question: Why must a prepared sterile field never be left unattended by the nurse?

options.A: Sterile drapes have a tendency to blow away in room drafts
options.B: Contamination can occur unnoticed if no one is watching the field
options.C: Hospital security regulations forbid empty treatment rooms
options.D: Patients might try to steal the surgical instruments

explanation: Leaving a field unsupervised risks unseen breaches in sterility, which compromises patient safety if used. [learn more](GNS311_U4_T1#GNS311_U4_T1_h6)

question: Which helpful acronym reminds nurses and clients of the warning signs for combined hormonal contraceptives?

options.A: ACHES
options.B: GATHER
options.C: ABCDE
options.D: SBAR

explanation: You got it! ACHES stands for Abdominal pain, Chest pain, Headaches, Eye problems, and Severe leg pain—key warning signs every pill user should watch out for. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T008#GNS226_U6_T008_h5)

question: A patient with stable COPD comes to the clinic asking about their daily routine. Which type of drug is best for long-term management?

options.A: An oral methylxanthine taken once a week
options.B: A long-acting bronchodilator taken every day
options.C: A short-acting rescue inhaler used every morning
options.D: An intravenous steroid given during clinic visits

explanation: For chronic conditions like COPD, consistency is key! Daily long-acting bronchodilators keep baseline symptoms under control so flare-ups happen less often. [learn more](GNS223_U2_T2#GNS223_U2_T2_h4)

question: What is considered the foundational duty of any healthcare manager?

options.A: Discipline
options.B: Budgeting
options.C: Planning
options.D: Delegation

explanation: Planning comes first because it sets the direction and goals for all other management duties like organizing and controlling. [learn more](GST321_U1_T7#GST321_U1_T7_h1)

question: Why should nurses care about population-focused public health prevention?
