explanation: Keeping your emotions in check and focusing on patient safety prevents the conflict from getting worse. [learn more](GST321_U7_T5#GST321_U7_T5_h7)

question: Why must a chest drainage system always stay lower than the patient's chest level?

options.A: To ensure the suction motor runs quietly without disturbing the patient
options.B: To use gravity effectively and prevent fluid from flowing backward into the pleural space
options.C: To make it easier for the patient to ambulate around the room
options.D: To prevent the water-seal chamber from evaporating too quickly

explanation: Gravity is our best friend here; keeping the collection box down ensures fluid drains away from the patient, not back into them. You've got a bright future in ward nursing! [learn more](GNS213_U2_T7#GNS213_U2_T7_h6)

question: As a nurse researcher, why would you choose to use qualitative interviews?

options.A: To measure exact physiological vital signs over time
options.B: To explore deep human experiences and personal perspectives
options.C: To test new pharmaceutical drugs on large populations
options.D: To calculate statistical averages of hospital stays

explanation: You've got this! Qualitative interviews are all about listening to patients' stories and feelings, rather than just crunching numbers. It's the human side of nursing research! [learn more](GNS224_U1_T24#GNS224_U1_T24_h1)

question: Why must a community diagnosis look at factors like housing and clean water?

options.A: These environmental factors directly shape the health outcomes of the population
options.B: Building codes are the legal responsibility of public health nurses
options.C: Hospital administrators require these statistics for annual budgeting
options.D: Doctors use these details to prescribe specific pharmaceutical drugs

explanation: Health is influenced by social, economic, and environmental conditions, not just medical care alone. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T1#GNS124_U3_T1_h1)

question: A nurse and a social worker disagree on how to discharge an elderly patient who lives alone. What should guide their next step?

options.A: Following the nurse's plan because nurses spend more time at the bedside
options.B: Letting the patient leave without any support services
options.C: Focusing on the patient's needs through shared decision-making
options.D: Escalating the disagreement to the hospital director immediately

explanation: Exactly! When team members see things differently, putting the patient's welfare first and talking it through always points the way forward. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T24#GNS225_U2_T24_h2)

question: What happens when you wash your hands and stop a germ from reaching a patient?

options.A: The reservoir completely disappears
options.B: The infectious agent instantly dies
options.C: A link in the chain of infection is broken
options.D: The patient becomes immune to all diseases

explanation: Spot on! Simple actions like hand hygiene interrupt transmission, effectively breaking the chain and keeping your patient safe. [learn more](GST114_U2_T1#GST114_U2_T1_h1)

question: Which of these is a common myth about infection control in home settings?

options.A: That handwashing helps reduce bacterial spread
options.B: That family members can transmit respiratory viruses
options.C: That the home environment is naturally germ-free
options.D: That used needles require special puncture-proof containers

explanation: Don't be fooled—homes are not naturally sterile! Good cleaning and hygiene habits are still a must everywhere. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T9#GNS324_U3_T9_h6)

question: Which client situation is a clear indication for a family planning referral?

options.A: A routine request for a three-month supply of injectable contraceptives
options.B: A first-time visit for condom distribution at a primary clinic
options.C: A simple request for general counseling on reproductive anatomy
options.D: A desire for a permanent surgical method like a vasectomy

explanation: Permanent surgical methods require specialized surgical skills not routinely offered at basic primary care posts. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T029#GNS226_U6_T029_h4)

question: Why does the nurse instruct the patient to empty their bladder right before the procedure begins?

options.A: To test the urine for hidden infection before the radiologist arrives
options.B: To make sure the patient does not need to use the restroom during the dye injection
options.C: To get an accurate baseline and prevent residual urine from blocking the view
options.D: To reduce the overall fluid volume inside the body before taking pictures

explanation: An empty bladder ensures that the initial images show the true anatomy without old urine diluting or obscuring the incoming contrast dye. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T3#GNS213_U4_T3_h4)

question: Why must pregnant women avoid eating raw or undercooked meats?

options.A: Raw meat causes severe allergic skin rashes in expectant mothers
options.B: Because cooked meat has more protein than raw meat
options.C: To prevent dangerous foodborne infections that can harm the pregnancy
options.D: Undercooked meat takes much longer for the stomach to digest

explanation: Raw meat can hide tricky germs and parasites like toxoplasma. Cooking food thoroughly keeps both mum and baby safe from infections! [learn more](GNS227_U2_T012#GNS227_U2_T012_h4)

question: What makes the rehabilitation nurse's role so special compared to a regular hospital nurse?

options.A: Nurses work completely in isolation without consulting other health professionals
options.B: It only involves administering intravenous medications on a strict schedule
options.C: It focuses heavily on helping clients adapt to long-term changes rather than just curing them
options.D: It completely replaces the need for physical and occupational therapy

explanation: Rehab nursing is less about quick fixes and more about walking side-by-side with patients as they adjust to long-term changes. Great nursing is heart work! [learn more](GNS314_U5_T2#GNS314_U5_T2_h1)

question: How can nurses help stop community members from hiding infectious illnesses out of fear?

options.A: Refusing to treat patients who do not speak English
options.B: Keeping all health information secret from local leaders
options.C: Threatening penalties for families that miss immunization days
options.D: Building trust through health education and supportive care

explanation: When we show empathy, educate gently, and create a safe space without judgment, community members feel comfortable coming to us early. [learn more](GNS313_U4_T4#GNS313_U4_T4_h7)

question: Why does the conjunctiva become easily inflamed during an infection?

options.A: It lacks any form of blood supply
options.B: It is directly exposed to the external environment
options.C: It produces thick, sticky tears
options.D: It contains heavy layers of bone

explanation: Because the conjunctiva lines the exposed outer surface of the eye and inner eyelids, it readily catches dust, germs, and allergens. [learn more](GNS211_U4_T1#GNS211_U4_T1_h1)

question: What is the main way our normal body flora protects us from harmful invaders?

options.A: It directly attacks and destroys human immune cells for food
options.B: It produces high levels of stomach acid to kill parasites
options.C: It prevents harmful pathogens from finding space and nutrients to grow
options.D: It accelerates the digestion of complex proteins in the stomach

explanation: This is called microbial antagonism! Because our friendly bacteria already occupy all the good parking spots and eat the available food, nasty new germs can't easily find a place to move in. [learn more](GST114_U3_T1#GST114_U3_T1_h5)

question: What should the nurse do immediately if a patient complains of severe burning under a poultice?

options.A: Wait another hour to see if it stops
options.B: Tie the bandage tighter to stop the burning
options.C: Tell the patient to endure the pain
options.D: Remove the poultice and wash the skin

explanation: Severe burning means the application is too hot or irritating, requiring immediate removal to prevent skin injury. [learn more](GNS221_U3_T10#GNS221_U3_T10_h7)

question: What was a major benefit when hospital-based home care programs first started?

options.A: They allowed patients to leave expensive hospital beds earlier while still receiving care
options.B: They completely eliminated the need for outpatient physician clinics
options.C: They removed all financial costs for the patients receiving treatment
options.D: They allowed nurses to perform major surgeries inside private residences

explanation: Extending hospital care into people's homes helped free up expensive hospital beds for sicker patients while keeping costs down. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T2#GNS324_U1_T2_h3)

question: What is the primary purpose of a health care budget?

options.A: To eliminate all unexpected hospital expenses permanently
options.B: To calculate exact salaries for individual doctors and nurses
options.C: To plan and control financial resources for medical services
options.D: To set the retail prices of medications in the pharmacy

explanation: A health care budget serves as a financial plan to guide how money is spent on patient care services. [learn more](GST322_U2_T4#GST322_U2_T4_h1)

question: Which of these is NOT a common barrier to changing health habits in local communities?

options.A: Cultural beliefs and traditional illness explanations
options.B: Poverty and severe economic hardship
options.C: Excessive availability of free clinical resources
options.D: Distrust of the formal healthcare system

explanation: Spot on! Having plenty of free resources helps health programs succeed. Poverty, cultural myths, and distrust are the real hurdles we face. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T3#GNS124_U5_T3_h6)

question: Why is it important to use local languages and traditional communication channels for immunization campaigns?

options.A: It prevents the government from spending money on printed books
options.B: It is required to qualify for international medical grants
options.C: It stops people from visiting traditional bone setters
options.D: It ensures the message is clearly understood and trusted by residents

explanation: Using familiar languages and traditional methods like town criers breaks down communication barriers and reduces fear. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T71#GNS214_U1_T71_h3)

question: When someone takes an NSAID like ibuprofen for a headache, which chemical messenger is blocked to stop the pain and swelling?

options.A: Adrenaline
options.B: Prostaglandins
options.C: Insulin
options.D: Histamines

explanation: Think of prostaglandins as the body's local alarm chemicals that trigger pain and swelling. NSAIDs block the enzymes that make them, giving you sweet relief! [learn more](GNS223_U5_T4#GNS223_U5_T4_h1)

question: Which of the following is NOT a common barrier to mental health referrals in Nigeria?

options.A: High cost of transportation and out-of-pocket treatment expenses
options.B: Poor communication and missing feedback letters between facilities
options.C: Stigma and initial reliance on traditional or spiritual healers
options.D: Immediate availability of fully equipped psychiatric units in every rural village

explanation: Spot the trick! Fully equipped psychiatric units in every rural village definitely do not exist, making this option the false statement—and thus the correct answer. [learn more](GNS314_U4_T4#GNS314_U4_T4_h6)

question: What is one of the most serious risks when an older adult suffers a fall?

options.A: Severe injury and potential loss of independence
options.B: Permanent immunity from future joint pain
options.C: Immediate improvement in their overall balance
options.D: An automatic increase in their muscle strength

explanation: Falls can lead to broken bones and a lasting fear of falling again, which often strips away an older adult's ability to care for themselves. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T3#GNS324_U3_T3_h5)

question: Which of these is an example of a research design rather than a tool?

options.A: A laboratory test tube used to check blood sugar
options.B: The overall structural framework of the study
options.C: A structured questionnaire handed to patients
options.D: An audio recording device used during an interview

explanation: Great job! The overall framework is your design, while items like questionnaires and test tubes are the physical tools you use inside that design. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T2#GNS224_U1_T2_h3)

question: Why should you gently clean and dry the skin before applying a fresh layer of medicated cream?

options.A: To remove old medication residue, sweat, and dirt that could block proper absorption
options.B: To test if the patient's skin is sensitive to water
options.C: To permanently sterilize the skin surface against all bacteria
options.D: To open up the pores so the skin absorbs the entire tube at once

explanation: Cleaning clears away old cream and sweat barriers so the fresh medicine can make direct contact with the skin. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T12#GNS215_U6_T12_h6)

question: Which scenario best shows a functioning financial safety net for someone with a physical disability?

options.A: Depending entirely on street begging
options.B: Selling household properties for emergency surgery
options.C: Borrowing from high-interest money lenders monthly
options.D: Receiving regular disability grants and healthcare subsidies from the state

explanation: A true safety net catches people so they don't fall into extreme poverty when health crises hit. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T12#GNS225_U5_T12_h5)

question: When a drainage tube gets blocked, which of these actions is completely WRONG and dangerous?

options.A: Pushing a partially dislodged tube back into the body cavity
options.B: Checking the entire length of the tubing for accidental kinks
options.C: Inspecting the tube for visible blood clots or mucus plugs
options.D: Notifying the medical team if output remains absent

explanation: You got it! Pushing a slipped tube back inside drags surface bacteria straight into sterile tissues. Always check with your senior or doctor first. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T22#GNS212_U1_T22_h6)

question: What happens during biological magnification (biomagnification) in a food chain?

options.A: Microbiological pathogens are neutralized by natural river currents
options.B: Fish grow larger and healthier due to the presence of mineral nutrients
options.C: Algae populations decrease rapidly due to cold water temperatures
options.D: Toxic chemicals become more concentrated in predators at higher trophic levels

explanation: Correct! As small creatures eat toxins and get eaten by bigger fish and animals, the poison multiplies and gets stronger higher up the food chain. [learn more](GST114_U6_T6#GST114_U6_T6_h5)

question: What is a common social double standard regarding the sexuality of adolescent boys and girls?

options.A: Girls are labeled immoral for sexual activity while boys are praised
options.B: Schools teach boys exclusively about menstruation and hygiene
options.C: Society expects girls to be sexually aggressive and dominant
options.D: Boys are denied clinic access while girls receive free medications

explanation: Sad but true—society often judges girls harshly for exploring their sexuality while treating the exact same behavior in boys as just a normal phase. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T11#GNS312_U3_T11_h3)

question: Why might a very stressed or anxious mum find it hard to express milk?

options.A: Stress permanently destroys the lactiferous ducts inside the breast
options.B: Anxiety causes the anterior pituitary to completely stop making prolactin
options.C: Nerve impulses from the nipple travel backward during panic attacks
options.D: Adrenaline constricts blood vessels and interferes with oxytocin release

explanation: You're doing great! Stress releases adrenaline, which gets in the way of oxytocin and makes the milk harder to let down. Relaxation is key! [learn more](GNS121_U5_T18#GNS121_U5_T18_h4)

question: At what exact times do we check the Apgar score for a newborn?

options.A: Every 30 minutes for the first two hours
options.B: At birth, 1 hour, and 6 hours of life
options.C: Right at birth and again at 10 minutes
options.D: At 1 minute and 5 minutes after birth

explanation: Remember the classic rule: Apgar is routinely checked at 1 minute of life, and then again at 5 minutes to track how the baby is adjusting. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T011#GNS226_U1_T011_h2)

question: When deciding on a study design, which of these is completely irrelevant?

options.A: Ethical boundaries regarding patient safety
options.B: Available financial resources and time
options.C: The specific research question being asked
options.D: The personal favorite color of the lead researcher

explanation: Haha, exactly! A researcher's favorite color has zero to do with science. Decisions are based purely on safety, questions, and resources. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T13#GNS217_U3_T13_h5)

question: How does progestin mainly prevent sperm from reaching an egg?

options.A: By destroying sperm in the vagina
options.B: By increasing the temperature of the uterus
options.C: By blocking the fallopian tubes physically
options.D: By thickening the cervical mucus

explanation: You've got this! Progestin changes the thickness of cervical fluid, creating a strong barrier that makes it very hard for sperm to swim upward. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T011#GNS226_U6_T011_h1)

question: Why is it important for nurses to use standard nutritional terms?

options.A: It allows nurses to cook meals for patients.
options.B: It prevents dangerous misunderstandings among the healthcare team.
options.C: It completely replaces the need for blood tests.
options.D: It speeds up the hospital discharge process.

explanation: Great job! Using clear, standard words means doctors, nurses, and dietitians are all on the same page, keeping your patients safe. [learn more](GNS227_U1_T001#GNS227_U1_T001_h1)

question: Which of these is NOT a normal challenge faced by public health institutions?

options.A: Excessive financial profits and private wealth accumulation
options.B: Bureaucratic delays in procuring medical supplies
options.C: Brain drain of experienced healthcare workers
options.D: Infrastructure decay and power supply failures

explanation: You nailed it! Public hospitals rarely swim in extra cash or private wealth; rather, they usually struggle with underfunding and resource shortages. [learn more](GST321_U10_T2#GST321_U10_T2_h5)

question: Why do nurses need to assist some patients with feeding?

options.A: To ensure adequate nutrition for patients who cannot feed themselves
options.B: To completely eliminate the risk of choking during every meal
options.C: To speed up meal times in busy hospital wards
options.D: To test the patient's swallowing reflexes before discharge

explanation: You've got this! Assisted feeding is simply stepping in to help patients who aren't able to eat on their own yet, making sure they get the strength they need. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T3#GNS212_U1_T3_h1)

question: A nurse researcher wants local ward staff to immediately adopt a new fall-prevention protocol. Which dissemination channel is most effective?

options.A: Publishing a brief note on a personal entertainment blog
options.B: Holding a hands-on clinical workshop and ward training session
options.C: Mailing hard copies of the raw data tables to the health minister
options.D: Submitting a lengthy letter to an international history journal

explanation: Hands-on workshops give frontline staff direct training and practice with new clinical protocols. [learn more](GNS224_U4_T2#GNS224_U4_T2_h4)

question: When is the best time for nurses to start teaching mothers about proper breastfeeding and preventing complications?

options.A: At the six-week postpartum checkup
options.B: During antenatal and early postnatal periods
options.C: Only after a breast abscess has formed
options.D: When the child is weaned to solid foods

explanation: Early teaching gives mothers the right techniques before any trouble starts. Prevention is always better than cure! [learn more](GNS226_U3_T025#GNS226_U3_T025_h7)

question: What is the main goal of using healthcare simulation in nursing education?

options.A: To safely bridge classroom theory with clinical practice
options.B: To replace traditional classroom lectures completely
options.C: To reduce the number of hours spent in real hospitals
options.D: To test students so they can be ranked in their class

explanation: Simulation gives students a bridge between what they read in books and the realities of caring for patients, all without any risk of harm. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T8#GNS212_U4_T8_h1)

question: Why are contaminated water sources such a huge public health worry?

options.A: They turn into live animal nests within a few hours
options.B: They stop antibiotics from working on skin cuts
options.C: They can quickly spread water germs to a whole lot of people at once
options.D: They automatically kill all the good bacteria in your tummy

explanation: Since everyone drinks water, a dirty water source can easily cause a massive community outbreak in no time. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T5#GNS313_U1_T5_h5)

question: Why is it so important for the body to keep producing hCG right after the embryo implants?

options.A: It directly softens the pelvic bones to prepare for eventual childbirth
options.B: It stimulates the fetal heart to begin beating inside the gestational sac
options.C: It forces the corpus luteum to keep producing progesterone and prevents menstruation
options.D: It stops the maternal immune system from ever recognizing the fetus

explanation: Spot on! hCG sends a vital signal to keep progesterone flowing, which stops the womb lining from shedding so the pregnancy can continue safely. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T2#GNS121_U6_T2_h5)

question: Which of these is NOT used to measure the quality of a nursing unit?

options.A: Patient fall rates and hospital-acquired infections
options.B: Medication error tracking and incident reports
options.C: Patient satisfaction survey scores
options.D: The favorite holiday destination of the nursing staff

explanation: You nailed it! Quality care is measured by safety outcomes and patient happiness, not personal staff trivia. [learn more](GST321_U6_T1#GST321_U6_T1_h7)

question: Before puberty starts, what does the central nervous system usually do regarding reproductive hormones?

options.A: It produces excess adult levels
options.B: It completely shuts down the pituitary
options.C: It suppresses hormone release
options.D: It secretes erratic daily spikes

explanation: You got it! Throughout childhood, the brain actively keeps reproductive hormone levels low and quiet until the body is mature enough for puberty. [learn more](GNS121_U4_T7#GNS121_U4_T7_h1)

question: When two rescuers are doing CPR on a child, what is the compression-to-ventilation ratio?

options.A: 5 compressions to 1 breath
options.B: 30 compressions to 2 breaths
options.C: 100 compressions to 5 breaths
options.D: 15 compressions to 2 breaths

explanation: When you have two people working together on a pediatric patient, you use a 15:2 ratio to get more rescue breaths into the child. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T3#GNS212_U2_T3_h3)

question: What is often the earliest warning sign of endometrial cancer in women who have gone through menopause?

options.A: Abnormal vaginal bleeding
options.B: Severe lower back pain
options.C: Rapid weight gain
options.D: Swollen lower extremities

explanation: Any spotting or bleeding after menopause is never normal and is usually the very first clue that prompts doctors to check the uterine lining. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T12#GNS311_U1_T12_h7)

question: A newborn is born limp, pale, and not breathing. What should be your very first immediate action in resuscitation?

options.A: Clear the airway and position the head correctly
options.B: Clamp and cut the cord immediately
options.C: Administer intravenous antibiotics right away
options.D: Weigh the baby on the delivery scale

explanation: Effective resuscitation begins with proper head positioning and clearing the airway to ensure air can enter the lungs. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T50#GNS214_U1_T50_h7)

question: What major risk goes up when a home care patient doesn't get enough protein and calories?

options.A: Excessive weight gain
options.B: Sudden permanent blindness
options.C: Rapid bone lengthening
options.D: Pressure injuries and delayed wound healing

explanation: Protein is like the building material for the body. Without enough of it, the skin breaks down easily and sores take forever to heal. Good nutrition is true medicine! [learn more](GNS324_U6_T1#GNS324_U6_T1_h2)

question: What is the primary function of a hormone receptor on a target cell?

options.A: To filter hormones out of the bloodstream
options.B: To manufacture and release new hormones
options.C: To break down excess hormones for energy
options.D: To recognize and bind a specific hormone

explanation: Receptors act like specialized locks that only open for their specific hormone key to trigger a cellular response. [learn more](GNS211_U1_T9#GNS211_U1_T9_h1)

question: Why are strong opioid painkillers usually avoided for routine home care after an abortion?

options.A: They carry high risks of sedation, nausea, and dependency
options.B: They permanently damage the lining of the stomach
options.C: They cause the uterus to stop contracting completely
options.D: They raise blood pressure to dangerously high levels

explanation: Routine cramps can usually be handled safely with milder drugs, sparing the patient from heavy side effects like sleepiness and nausea. Makes total sense! [learn more](GNS226_U5_T014#GNS226_U5_T014_h3)

question: What happens in your body during the normal urination reflex?

options.A: The ureters close tightly to push extra fluid backward.
options.B: The transitional epithelium absorbs all the leftover fluid.
options.C: The detrusor muscle contracts and the internal sphincter relaxes.
options.D: The detrusor muscle relaxes and both sphincters tighten.

explanation: Spot on! Urination is a team effort: the bladder wall squeezes (detrusor contracts) while the doorway opens up (internal sphincter relaxes). [learn more](GNS121_U2_T3#GNS121_U2_T3_h5)

question: Who is most likely to act as the primary day-to-day caregiver for a patient recovering at home?

options.A: Family members living with or near the client
options.B: The contracted medical equipment delivery driver
options.C: Voluntary auditors from the federal government
options.D: The regional health commissioner on duty

explanation: That's right! In our setting, family is everything. Loved ones usually do the heavy lifting of supporting patients between our visits. [learn more](GNS324_U2_T1#GNS324_U2_T1_h3)

question: A patient arrives at your clinic with confirmed Lassa fever. Which reporting category does this fall under?

options.A: Category 3
options.B: Category 2
options.C: Category 1
options.D: Category 5

explanation: You nailed it! Because Lassa fever is a severe viral illness that can spread quickly, it's treated as a Category 1 emergency. [learn more](GST114_U2_T20#GST114_U2_T20_h3)

question: Why is it important to carefully inspect the removed threads and the incision site?

options.A: To ensure no small pieces of thread were left inside the skin
options.B: To count the exact number of stitches for insurance records
options.C: To prove to the patient that the procedure is finished
options.D: To save the old thread pieces for laboratory testing

explanation: Retained suture fragments act as foreign bodies that can trigger a delayed local infection or inflammatory reaction inside the tissue. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T12#GNS122_U2_T12_h6)

question: Why do nurses use the 'teach-back' method after giving health instructions?

options.A: Testing the patient's memory span after a long hospital stay
options.B: Checking if the patient truly understands the dietary instructions
options.C: Giving the nurse a break from talking during the clinic visit
options.D: Fulfilling mandatory legal paperwork requirements for discharge

explanation: Spot on! Having the patient explain things back in their own words is the safest way to ensure they truly understand. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T004#GNS227_U7_T004_h6)

question: What are the three main phases that make up the peri-operative timeline?

options.A: Admission, treatment, and discharge
options.B: Preparation, surgery, and rehabilitation
options.C: Assessment, intervention, and evaluation
options.D: Pre-operative, intra-operative, and post-operative

explanation: Peri-operative care encompasses the entire surgical experience, which is divided sequentially into before, during, and after the operation. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T10#GNS123_U5_T10_h1)

question: How does pharmacokinetic antagonism affect drug levels in a patient's body?

options.A: By binding permanently to every receptor in the nervous system
options.B: By changing the electrical charge of the red blood cells
options.C: By increasing the metabolism or excretion of the other drug
options.D: By stopping the kidneys from producing any urine output

explanation: One drug makes the body break down or flush out the other drug faster, leaving less active medicine floating around. Makes total sense when you break it down! [learn more](GNS125_U5_T7#GNS125_U5_T7_h5)

question: Why do patients taking anticholinergics often end up with constipation?

options.A: Abdominal muscles become paralyzed by the drug
options.B: The medication slows down gastrointestinal motility
options.C: The drug pulls water directly out of the stool
options.D: Bile production in the liver is completely stopped

explanation: Just like it slows down the bladder, the drug also slows down movement in the gut. Less movement means sluggish bowels! [learn more](GNS223_U8_T5#GNS223_U8_T5_h5)

question: What is the very first thing a nurse should do for a patient going into shock from severe post-abortion bleeding?

options.A: Perform a detailed psychosocial history regarding the pregnancy
options.B: Send the patient immediately for diagnostic pelvic ultrasound
options.C: Administer oral rehydration salts and counsel on contraception
options.D: Insert large-bore intravenous lines for fluid resuscitation

explanation: ABC comes first—and in bleeding shock, getting IV lines open fast to pump fluids and restore blood volume is an absolute lifesaver! You've got this. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T002#GNS226_U5_T002_h4)

question: Which organ function must a nurse check before a patient starts a direct oral anticoagulant?

options.A: Renal clearance and function
options.B: Hepatic enzyme production
options.C: Gastric acid secretion rate
options.D: Pulmonary ventilation capacity

explanation: Since these drugs leave the body through the kidneys, checking kidney function first keeps the patient safe from drug buildup. You've got this! [learn more](GNS215_U6_T14#GNS215_U6_T14_h5)

question: What kind of muscle action drives the final expulsion phase of ejaculation?

options.A: Rhythmic skeletal muscle contractions
options.B: Voluntary cardiac muscle pulsations
options.C: Involuntary glandular cell secretion
options.D: Slow, continuous smooth muscle peristalsis

explanation: You're doing great! Quick, automatic squeezes from your pelvic skeletal muscles are what power the final exit. [learn more](GNS121_U4_T5#GNS121_U4_T5_h4)

question: Why do nurses need to look at social services alongside medical care?

options.A: Medical treatments are completely ineffective without prior social assessment.
options.B: Patient recovery and well-being depend heavily on social and economic factors outside the hospital.
options.C: Nurses are legally required to distribute government welfare grants directly.
options.D: Hospital management mandates that nurses handle all community social work.

explanation: Medical care is only one piece of the puzzle! Factors like a patient's home, income, and community support play a massive role in how well and how fast they heal. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T16#GNS225_U5_T16_h1)

question: Which body sets the professional standards and scope of practice for nurses in Nigeria?

options.A: Civil Service Commission of the Federation
options.B: Nigerian Medical Association Secretariat
options.C: Nursing and Midwifery Council of Nigeria
options.D: Federal Ministry of Labour and Productivity

explanation: The Nursing and Midwifery Council of Nigeria (NMCN) is our main regulatory body. They set the training rules and standards we all follow as nurses. [learn more](GST321_U10_T1#GST321_U10_T1_h2)

question: Which of these medications is considered a minor tranquilizer?

options.A: Chlorpromazine
options.B: Risperidone
options.C: Diazepam
options.D: Haloperidol

explanation: Diazepam is a benzodiazepine, which doctors commonly use as a minor tranquilizer to help calm anxiety. Great practice for your pharmacology exams! [learn more](GNS223_U6_T4#GNS223_U6_T4_h2)

question: Which of these is a classic long-term heart problem tied to heavy, chronic drinking?

options.A: Permanent stabilization of heart valves
options.B: Cardiomyopathy and hypertension
options.C: Significantly lowered resting pulse rate
options.D: Increased production of red blood cells

explanation: Over time, heavy drinking weakens the heart muscle (cardiomyopathy) and drives up blood pressure (hypertension). Take care of that ticker! [learn more](GNS227_U4_T013#GNS227_U4_T013_h4)

question: Why must a nurse position a patient upright before giving oral medications?

options.A: It speeds up the first-pass metabolism in the liver
options.B: It allows the nurse to check the pulse more easily
options.C: Gravity helps the medication go down safely and prevents choking
options.D: It stops the stomach acid from rising into the throat

explanation: Sitting at a 90-degree angle uses gravity to guide the pill into the esophagus and protects the airway from accidental aspiration. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T14#GNS122_U1_T14_h2)

question: Why is localized swelling and extra blood flow actually a good thing when you have an infection?

options.A: It prevents any fluid from entering the damaged tissue spaces
options.B: It stops all cellular activity so the body can rest completely
options.C: It lowers local body temperature to kill heat-sensitive viruses
options.D: It brings white blood cells quickly to the site to fight invaders

explanation: Swelling and extra blood flow aren't just uncomfortable; they are high-speed delivery routes rushing white blood cells straight to the battlefield to clear out germs. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T14#GNS111_U2_T14_h5)

question: What is the main benefit of placing a severe COVID-19 patient in the prone position (lying on their stomach)?

options.A: It improves oxygen exchange and lung expansion
options.B: It completely eliminates the need for intravenous lines
options.C: It prevents the patient from coughing during sleep
options.D: It allows the patient to feed themselves more easily

explanation: Well done! Gravity helps open up parts of the lungs that are pressed down when lying on the back, making it much easier for the patient to get oxygen. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T6#GNS123_U4_T6_h7)

question: Why is 'recency error' a bad thing during an annual nursing review?

options.A: It forces the manager to use outdated hospital policies from years ago
options.B: It ignores months of good or bad work and focuses only on recent events
options.C: It requires the nurse to memorize every shift worked in the past month
options.D: It increases the time needed to complete the final paperwork

explanation: It's unfair to judge a whole year of hard work based only on what happened in the last two weeks. Managers need to look at the big picture! [learn more](GST321_U1_T21#GST321_U1_T21_h4)

question: What does 'observed frequency' mean in a Chi-Square study?

options.A: The actual data counts collected from the sample
options.B: The total number of variables in the study
options.C: The level of significance chosen by the researcher
options.D: The theoretical counts expected under the null hypothesis

explanation: You got it! Observed frequencies are the real-life numbers you gather directly from your surveys, forms, or patients. [learn more](GNS217_U4_T13#GNS217_U4_T13_h5)

question: Which of the following is an example of a long-acting reversible contraceptive method?

options.A: A subdermal hormonal implant
options.B: A packet of daily oral contraceptive pills
options.C: Spermicidal foam applied before sex
options.D: Male latex condoms used during intercourse

explanation: Implants and intrauterine devices are classified as LARC methods because they work continuously for years without daily action from the user. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T015#GNS226_U5_T015_h4)
